title: Git-free pipeline
prompt: A team has three preexisting Fabric workspaces (Dev/Test/Prod) and a change-control board. Security policy forbids connecting any of them to Git, but the team must promote supported workspace items with stage comparison. Which design is viable? (Select one answer.)

options.text: Use an Azure DevOps Git branch for each target because stage comparisons read repository branches.
options.why: Incorrect: deployment compares items in workspace stages, not Git branches.

options.text: Create one Git repository and connect only Dev because the first stage must be synchronized.
options.why: Incorrect: Git is optional even for Dev.

options.text: Create a deployment pipeline, assign one workspace per stage, compare and deploy selected items.
options.why: Correct: deployment pipelines work independently of Git.

options.text: Use Git commits only; workspace-to-workspace deployment is unavailable without source control.
options.why: Incorrect: this confuses CI with Fabric deployment pipelines.

explanation: Deployment pipelines implement promotion between assigned workspaces independently of Git integration. Git is complementary version control, not an execution prerequisite.

title: Uncommitted workspace changes
prompt: A Dev workspace is connected to Azure DevOps. The latest repository commit defines notebook revision 4, but a developer has unsynchronized notebook revision 5 saved in Dev. A release manager deploys Dev to Test without updating from Git. What is the source of the deployment? (Select one answer.)

options.text: The notebook in Test remains unmodified because Git tracks an older version.
options.why: Incorrect: Git status alone does not stop deployment.

options.text: Revision 4, because deployment pipelines resolve the source repository HEAD first.
options.why: Incorrect: no implicit Git read occurs.

options.text: No notebook can deploy until every Git change is committed and synced.
options.why: Incorrect: Git cleanliness is not a pipeline prerequisite.

options.text: Revision 5 as currently represented in the Dev workspace, subject to support and selected scope.
options.why: Correct: the source is the Fabric workspace state.

explanation: Git integration versions definitions; deployment pipelines compare and promote the source-stage workspace content at deployment time. Enforce a separate release gate if only committed changes may deploy.

options.text: At most three are possible, so QA and UAT must be outside the pipeline.
